# Third-party software

CyberdyneEngine integrates the software listed here. Each dependency sits behind an engine-owned
interface, is pinned to an exact commit, and carries a permissive licence — the conditions
`thirdparty-dependencies` sets for adopting one at all.

The tables after the first are different kinds of entry and each says so where it starts: software a
contributor's machine must provide for one tool-time step, which the engine never fetches, links or
redistributes; and the editor's Rust crates, which are acquired by Cargo and linked into the editor
alone.

<!-- Generated by tools/deps/attribution.py from deps/manifest.toml, deps/host-tools.toml and
     deps/rust-crates.toml. Do not edit: run `just maintenance-deps` instead. CI fails when this
     file and the manifests disagree. -->

## What a build actually links

A dependency with a gating option is fetched, built and linked **only** when that option is on. A
build with the option off contains none of its code, so the notices it requires do not apply to
that build. The engine's runtime attribution reports the set for the build in hand rather than this
whole table.

| Dependency | Version | Licence | Included when | Links into |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [sdl3](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL) | 3.4.16 | Zlib | always | a shipped game |
| [doctest](https://github.com/doctest/doctest) | 2.4.12 | MIT | `CY_BUILD_TESTS` is on | the test binaries only |
| [tracy](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy) | 0.12.2 | BSD-3-Clause | `CY_PROFILING` is on | development builds only |
| [zstd](https://github.com/facebook/zstd) | 1.5.7 | BSD-3-Clause | always | a shipped game |
| [blake3](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3) | 1.8.7 | CC0-1.0 | always | a shipped game |
| [vulkan_headers](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Headers) | 1.4.304 | Apache-2.0 | `CY_RENDERER_VULKAN` is on | a shipped game |
| [volk](https://github.com/zeux/volk) | 1.4.304 | MIT | `CY_RENDERER_VULKAN` is on | a shipped game |

## Host prerequisites, which are not linked and not shipped

These are **not** part of any artefact the engine produces. They are software that has to be present
on a contributor's machine for one tool-time step — parsing annotated C++ to regenerate reflection
metadata — and the engine neither fetches, links, nor redistributes them. They are listed because
`thirdparty-dependencies` asks for a complete record of third-party software the project depends on,
and because a prerequisite nobody declared is one a fresh clone discovers by failing.

The generated metadata is committed, so a clone builds and tests without any of these; only
regeneration needs them, and `just generate-check` is what notices.

| Prerequisite | Version | Licence | Kind | Needed for | Install |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [clang](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project) | 18.1.8 | Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception | python-package | `just generate-check` | `pip install --user clang==18.1.8` |
| [libclang1-18](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project) | 18 | Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception | system-library | `just generate-check` | `sudo apt install libclang1-18` |
| [rust 1.95.0, with rustfmt and clippy](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust) | 1.95.0 | Apache-2.0 OR MIT | toolchain | `just build-editor` | `rustup toolchain install 1.95.0` |

### sdl3 3.4.16

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL
- **Pinned at**: `fa2c02bb6e21974a89ea9824bc53c9932abe5f9c` (`release-3.4.16`)
- **Licence**: Zlib
- **Licence text**: [`LICENSE.txt`](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/fa2c02bb6e21974a89ea9824bc53c9932abe5f9c/LICENSE.txt), and
  `LICENSE.txt` at the root of the fetched source in any configured build tree
- **Behind**: cy::Platform and cy::DisplayServer, implemented in platform/desktop-sdl3/
- **Included when**: always
- **Linked into**: a shipped game
- **Why integrated rather than built**: Window, event, and gamepad coverage across three desktop platforms, plus the controller database, which is maintenance rather than differentiation.

### doctest 2.4.12

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/doctest/doctest
- **Pinned at**: `1da23a3e8119ec5cce4f9388e91b065e20bf06f5` (`v2.4.12`)

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Headers

### volk 1.4.304

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/zeux/volk
- **Pinned at**: `0b17a763ba5643e32da1b2152f8140461b3b7345` (`1.4.304`)
- **Licence**: MIT
- **Licence text**: [`LICENSE.md`](https://github.com/zeux/volk/blob/0b17a763ba5643e32da1b2152f8140461b3b7345/LICENSE.md), and
  `LICENSE.md` at the root of the fetched source in any configured build tree
- **Behind**: cy::rhi in src/backends/rhi/vulkan/, which is the only directory that names a Vulkan symbol
- **Included when**: `CY_RENDERER_VULKAN` is on
- **Linked into**: a shipped game
- **Why integrated rather than built**: A meta-loader: entry points are fetched per device rather than through the loader's dispatch trampoline, which removes a per-call indirection and lets the engine link no Vulkan library at all. Writing one is a generated-code maintenance task with no differentiation in it.

### vma 3.3.0

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator
- **Pinned at**: `1d8f600fd424278486eade7ed3e877c99f0846b1` (`v3.3.0`)
- **Licence**: MIT
- **Licence text**: [`LICENSE.txt`](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator/blob/1d8f600fd424278486eade7ed3e877c99f0846b1/LICENSE.txt), and
  `LICENSE.txt` at the root of the fetched source in any configured build tree
- **Behind**: the RHI's memory report and transient pool in src/backends/rhi/vulkan/; GPU bytes reach the engine through cy::MemoryDomain::Gpu and the shared pressure monitor, not through a second report
- **Included when**: `CY_RENDERER_VULKAN` is on
- **Linked into**: a shipped game
- **Why integrated rather than built**: Suballocation, memory-type selection, defragmentation and VK_EXT_memory_budget tracking against a device's own heaps. An allocator is not differentiating and getting memory types wrong is a class of bug that only appears on the vendor nobody tested.

### slang 2026.9.2

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/shader-slang/slang
- **Pinned at**: `5ad2bcb74902fa5cf4344e9ee3dd33fa125883cb` (`v2026.9.2`)
- **Licence**: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
- **Licence text**: [`LICENSE`](https://github.com/shader-slang/slang/blob/5ad2bcb74902fa5cf4344e9ee3dd33fa125883cb/LICENSE), and
  `LICENSE` at the root of the fetched source in any configured build tree
- **Behind**: cy::shader::ShaderCompiler in src/backends/shader/slang/, which is the only directory that names a Slang symbol; the pipeline around it consumes SPIR-V
- **Included when**: `CY_SHADER_SLANG` is on
- **Linked into**: the editor and the cooker only
- **Why integrated rather than built**: The authoring language `shader-system` adopts, and the compiler that lowers it to SPIR-V. Writing a shading language is a multi-year commitment that competes directly with building the renderer; Slang supplies generics, interfaces, modules and multi-target output and is designed for exactly this use.

### recast 1.6.0

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/recastnavigation/recastnavigation
- **Pinned at**: `6dc1667f580357e8a2154c28b7867bea7e8ad3a7` (`v1.6.0`)
- **Licence**: Zlib
- **Licence text**: [`License.txt`](https://github.com/recastnavigation/recastnavigation/blob/6dc1667f580357e8a2154c28b7867bea7e8ad3a7/License.txt), and

- **Included when**: `CY_NAVIGATION` is on
- **Linked into**: a shipped game
- **Why integrated rather than built**: Voxelising source geometry and extracting walkable convex regions — the one navigation step `ai-system` names as not differentiating, and `navigation` specifies procedurally in Recast's own parameters: cell size and height, agent radius, height, climb and slope, region minimum and merge sizes, edge length and error, detail sample distance and error. It is the reference implementation of that algorithm and the alternative is a marching-squares research project. Detour is excluded by source_subdir; the runtime mesh, the queries, the hierarchy, flow fields, avoidance and crowds are engine code.

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio
- **Pinned at**: `0da18255cca520771f363ee01f100572b39a308e` (`v4.8.1`)
- **Licence**: Apache-2.0

### clang 18.1.8

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project
- **Licence**: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception ([`clang/LICENSE.TXT`](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project))
- **Kind**: python-package, provided by the host — never fetched, never linked, never redistributed
- **Loaded by**: `tools/gen/reflect/parse.py`
- **Absence is caught by**: `just generate-check`, and reported by `just env-doctor`
- **Install**: `pip install --user clang==18.1.8` (Linux), `pip install --user clang==18.1.8` (macOS),
  `pip install --user clang==18.1.8` (Windows)
- **Why a host prerequisite rather than a fetched dependency**: core-type-system requires annotated C++ to be parsed with a real C++ frontend rather than a text scanner. These are the upstream bindings to that frontend; they are a tool-time interface to a library the host provides and enter no artefact the engine ships.

### libclang1-18 18

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project
- **Licence**: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception ([`clang/LICENSE.TXT`](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project))
- **Kind**: system-library, provided by the host — never fetched, never linked, never redistributed
- **Loaded by**: `tools/gen/reflect/parse.py`
- **Absence is caught by**: `just generate-check`, and reported by `just env-doctor`
- **Install**: `sudo apt install libclang1-18` (Linux), `brew install llvm@18` (macOS),
  `winget install LLVM.LLVM` (Windows)
- **Why a host prerequisite rather than a fetched dependency**: The C++ frontend the bindings above load. Taken from the host rather than fetched because building LLVM is hours of build time for a library only the generator uses, and every supported platform packages it.

### rust 1.95.0, with rustfmt and clippy 1.95.0

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust
- **Licence**: Apache-2.0 OR MIT ([`LICENSE-APACHE`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust))
- **Kind**: toolchain, provided by the host — never fetched, never linked, never redistributed
- **Loaded by**: `rust-toolchain.toml`
- **Absence is caught by**: `just build-editor`, and reported by `just env-doctor`
- **Install**: `rustup toolchain install 1.95.0` (Linux), `rustup toolchain install 1.95.0` (macOS),
  `rustup toolchain install 1.95.0` (Windows)
- **Why a host prerequisite rather than a fetched dependency**: The editor is a Rust application, and 1.95.0 is a hard minimum rather than a preference: the interface toolkit M5.5 selected does not compile below it. The toolchain is taken from the host because a compiler is not something a build fetches, and it is pinned rather than floating so that a compiler release is a reviewed change like every other dependency.

## The editor's Rust crates

The editor is a separate binary and a separate dependency set: none of this is linked into a game,
and a packaged game contains no part of it. It is listed here because `thirdparty-dependencies`
governs the editor's Rust dependencies under the same policy as the engine's C++ ones, and because
386 crates that appear in no attribution document are 386 crates nobody has reviewed.

11 were chosen; each is named in `editor/Cargo.toml`, sits behind the editor's own
abstractions, and carries the argument for its adoption below. The other 375 arrived
through those 11, which is the transitive cost `thirdparty-dependencies` requires to be part
of the decision rather than a discovery. Every one of them is pinned by `editor/Cargo.lock` — an
exact version and a registry checksum — and recorded with its licence in `deps/rust-crates.toml`.

Where a crate offers a choice of licences, the project takes a permissive one; the record is the
expression its author published.

## Notices — the editor crates that were chosen

### ash 0.38.0+1.3.281

- **Upstream**: https://crates.io/crates/ash
- **Pinned at**: `0.38.0+1.3.281`, checksum `0bb44936d800fea8f016d7f2311c6a4f97aebd5dc86f09906139ec848cf3a46f` in `editor/Cargo.lock`
- **Licence**: MIT OR Apache-2.0
- **Named by**: `cy-editor-viewport-transport`
- **Linked into**: the editor only — no part of it enters a packaged game
- **Why integrated rather than built**: The Vulkan API where wgpu does not expose it — timeline semaphore import and export, the bounded host wait, and the DRM format-modifier queries the cross-process viewport needs. Behind cy-editor-viewport-transport, which is the only crate that names it.

### eframe 0.36.1

- **Upstream**: https://crates.io/crates/eframe
- **Pinned at**: `0.36.1`, checksum `2afc0cbcdb6896b7bfb1dbbebaf7b9af9635ff38fd01e89bdd0174c1717b1857` in `editor/Cargo.lock`
- **Licence**: MIT OR Apache-2.0
- **Named by**: `cy-editor-shell`
- **Linked into**: the editor only — no part of it enters a packaged game
- **Why integrated rather than built**: The window, the event loop and the wgpu renderer beneath the interface toolkit, with AccessKit — which editor-ui-ux requires and which decided the toolkit. Behind cy-editor-shell, and a containment test keeps it there.

### egui 0.36.1

- **Upstream**: https://crates.io/crates/egui
- **Pinned at**: `0.36.1`, checksum `c977ac91dfaa651633fd9722e4ce9ccb32cda4c748b89a5cb57e504036e37c13` in `editor/Cargo.lock`
- **Licence**: MIT OR Apache-2.0
- **Named by**: `cy-editor-shell`
- **Linked into**: the editor only — no part of it enters a packaged game
- **Why integrated rather than built**: The immediate-mode interface toolkit, selected on measurement per editor-rust-application and kept replaceable behind the editor's own view models: no toolkit type appears in the document, command, protocol or plugin-facing layers.

### pollster 0.4.0

### wgpu 30.0.1

- **Upstream**: https://crates.io/crates/wgpu
- **Pinned at**: `30.0.1`, checksum `527ccdf43dd5b2e8676eed9984ce00e2bbb0a1b85b70c1969dcb6cd2eb55ab9e` in `editor/Cargo.lock`

### wgpu-hal 30.0.1

- **Upstream**: https://crates.io/crates/wgpu-hal
